findings.problem: SampleWorkflow allows any combination of status string, lifecycle booleans, and optional timestamp. Validating combinations are unreachable (is_sent=true with sent_at_epoch_ms=None), and invalid combinations like is_validated=false with is_sent=true compile and run silently.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can construct a SampleWorkflow that violates domain invariants. The type system gives zero protection against impossible state: marked-as-sent with no timestamp, not-validated but marked-sent, or a status string not matching any lifecycle boolean.
findings.fix: Replace status: String plus is_validated: bool / is_sent: bool with a single enum WorkflowState { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }. Remove the separate booleans and optional timestamp. Construction via a single smart constructor enforces invariants at compile time.

findings.problem: status: String combined with is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool creates an explosion of reachable states (3 strings x 2 x 2 = 12), most of which are meaningless. The status string and booleans are redundant and mutually inconsistent by design.
findings.failure_mode: Pattern matching on status string yields unreachable arms. Comparing booleans yields inconsistent results. Adding a new status requires updating three independent fields correctly.
findings.fix: Replace all three fields with a single enum WorkflowState with variants for each lifecycle stage. Put optional lifecycle data (sent_at_epoch_ms) inside the variant that owns it.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive that carries no domain constraints. Any string value, empty string, or malformed ID is accepted with zero validation.
findings.failure_mode: Empty string IDs, duplicate IDs, or IDs exceeding domain bounds pass through unchecked. Core logic cannot assume id validity without revalidating at every use site.
findings.fix: Use a newtype Id(String) or Id([u8; N]) with a smart constructor that validates and returns a typed error. Core logic consumes Id, never raw String for identity.

findings.problem: mark_sent sets status and is_sent but does NOT set sent_at_epoch_ms, leaving a sent item with no timestamp. It also does not verify the precondition that the item was validated before being sent.
findings.failure_mode: An item can be marked as sent without ever being validated, and with no sent_at_epoch_ms timestamp. Downstream code reading sent_at_epoch_ms gets None and must handle it, or the invariant 'sent items have timestamps' is silently broken.
findings.fix: With the enum typestate approach, sent_at_epoch_ms becomes part of the Sent variant and is required at construction. mark_sent should be replaced by a state-transition function or smart constructor that takes the prior state and returns the next state, making transitions compile-time enforced.

findings.problem: There is no constructor, smart constructor, or parse boundary for SampleWorkflow. Any caller can call SampleWorkflow { id: "".into(), status: "blah".into(), is_validated: false, is_sent: true, sent_at_epoch_ms: None } and the code compiles.
findings.failure_mode: Domain invariants are enforced nowhere. External callers, tests, and the core itself can construct invalid states. No typed error is returned for invalid input.
findings.fix: Add a private constructor or a factory function SampleWorkflow::new(...) -> Result<SampleWorkflow, WorkflowError> that validates all invariants. Make fields private and expose only through methods.

findings.problem: All fields of SampleWorkflow are pub, allowing external mutation of any field without going through an API method. This bypasses any invariant enforcement.
findings.failure_mode: A caller can do item.is_validated = false after mark_sent(item), re-opening a sent workflow. The struct has no encapsulation barrier.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Expose behavior through methods on the struct. With an enum typestate, the type itself prevents invalid mutation.

findings.problem: mark_sent returns SampleWorkflow directly with no error type. There is no WorkflowError enum for expected domain failures (e.g., cannot send unvalidated item, item already sent).
findings.failure_mode: Error conditions must be communicated via panic, Option, or a String error — none of which are railway-friendly. Callers cannot pattern-match on expected failure modes.
findings.fix: Return Result<SampleWorkflow, WorkflowError> where WorkflowError is an enum with typed variants like AlreadySent, NotValidated, InvalidState(String). The enum typestate approach makes some of these unreachable at compile time.

findings.problem: No benchmark exists for any performance-relevant path. The crate has zero performance evidence despite marking items and managing workflow state.
findings.failure_mode: Cannot verify that workflow operations meet latency or throughput requirements. Allocation patterns (to_string on every mark_sent) are unmeasured.
findings.fix: Add a criterion or tiny_bench benchmark for mark_sent and any hot-path operations.

findings.problem: No proptest, Kani, Miri, or invariant test evidence. The struct invariants (sent implies timestamp, validated before sent) are untested programmatically.
findings.failure_mode: No automated proof or property-based testing that invariants hold across state transitions. Invalid states can be introduced by refactoring with zero detection.
findings.fix: Add proptest properties: sent implies has timestamp, validated precedes sent, status enum exhaustiveness. Run cargo clippy -- -D warnings before claiming clean.

findings.problem: No test module exists. mark_sent behavior is untested. Invalid state construction is untested.
findings.failure_mode: Regression in mark_sent or workflow state machine will not be detected. New callers can introduce invalid states without test coverage.
findings.fix: Add tests for: valid lifecycle transitions, invalid transition rejection, enum exhaustiveness.

findings.problem: mark_sent allocates a new String via "sent".to_string() on every call. With the enum typestate approach, the status field would be an enum variant (zero-allocation).
findings.failure_mode: Every state transition allocates a heap String. In high-throughput workflows, this is measurable overhead. The sent_at_epoch_ms allocation (Option<u64> is cheap, but the String is not).
findings.fix: Replace status String with an enum variant. The typestate enum has no heap allocation for status representation. If id must remain String, consider if &str parameter is sufficient for the operation.

findings.problem: If mark_sent were changed to return Result<_, _>, callers could silently discard the result with let _ = mark_sent(...). However, as-is the function returns a value directly.
findings.failure_mode: Future changes to return Result without #[must_use] allow silent error suppression.
findings.fix: When introducing Result return, add #[must_use] to the error type.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent or any workflow operation
no proptest or property-based tests for invariants
no Kani/Miri execution for state-transition safety
residual_risk: Static review only. No commands were run. The core issue is architectural: SampleWorkflow makes illegal states representable through primitive fields (String status + bool flags + Option<u64>). This is the single highest-severity finding — replacing the struct with an enum typestate resolves the majority of BLOCKER and MAJOR findings simultaneously. Until this refactoring is done, any downstream code inherits the invalid-state problem.
